pillar_reactions.evidence: Accepted the substance — 'it's consistent with what he's been saying in everything I've listened to' — but then asked a mechanics question about load selection: 'Some kettlebell exercises, obviously, I can't do the same weight, but other ones, you feel like the swings, you feel like you could do more. But in the videos, he seems to be using the same kettlebell for everything.' The rep answered with individualisation: 'we cannot have the same program for a 20-year-old athlete and a 60-year-old former athlete.'

Flagged it as the unknown before the rep presented it — 'that's one thing he hasn't talked too much about, so be interested to hear about how this part worked' — and then checked the mechanic against the coach's own practice: 'But you're saying that he does follow this eight-hour window?' Closed with 'No, I think I understand.'

Tied it to his own history unprompted: 'one thing about me is, you know, I have accountability. So when I feel like I'm accountable to somebody or something, I seem to do it more', and explained why the old paid group classes worked — 'you signed up and you're taking a spot away from somebody else. I had to show up, otherwise they'd freak out on you.' He also corrected the rep's framing to sharpen it: 'I mean, I do need accountability, so I think it's good to be held accountable.'

anchors.raw: I started looking at Trevor's, um, Instagram and started doing kettlebells. So now I pretty much follow what he's, what he shares online. Um, and I, you know, I really, I like it.
anchors.note: The strongest anchor on the call is Primal's own marketing. He has been running the method free for two months and reports it working — 'I've seen my arms and everything, my change since I've been doing the kettlebells' — so the $6,000 has to be justified against a substitute the company itself supplies at zero cost. His exit line was 'I'll keep using Trevor's videos.'

anchors.raw: for about two or three years, I was paying $300 a month at this gym and I was doing HIIT training, which with the class like no bigger than 10 people. And I liked it, the camaraderie and everything, but it just got too expensive.
anchors.note: $300/month is his ceiling for supervised, accountable training, and he already walked away from it on cost. $6,000 over six months is $1,000/month — more than triple the price he already judged too expensive.

anchors.raw: So I joined the gym in January with my wife, which is like a third of the price.
anchors.note: Implies roughly $100/month, and it is a joint household spend with his wife. Sets the live reference point for what fitness costs in his budget.

anchors.raw: On the 2-3 range, that's what I was thinking, so.
anchors.note: He arrived with a $2,000-$3,000 ceiling already formed, which is roughly a third to half the offer. Worth tracing back to the setter call — nothing in the transcript suggests price was pre-framed before he got on with the closer.

unmet_demand.want: A structured, coached kettlebell programme at somewhere between $2,000 and $3,000
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The stated offer starts at $6,000 for six months. The rep improvised a $4,000 three-month tier to reach for it, which still sat above the ceiling and raised the monthly rate from $1,000 to $1,333.

unmet_demand.want: The obligation mechanic of a booked group class — being missed by name if he does not show
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme's accountability is one-to-one and asynchronous through an app plus a weekly check-in. The rep acknowledged the difference directly: 'it's not a group environment, but definitely there's a big part of accountability and Trevor will call you out if you're going to be missing your workouts.'

unmet_demand.want: Reassurance that a six-month commitment fits an evening-constrained schedule in a different time zone to the coach
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Nothing structural blocks it — the programme is asynchronous — but the prospect raised it as a real hesitation ('the time zone differences, does that cause an issue? Because my availability is tighter at night than it is during the day') and it was answered in passing rather than resolved.
